title: A dominant morphism of integral curves with finite generic extension is quasi-finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ and $E$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated schemes of finite type over $k$, each of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $p:E\to C$ be a dominant $k$-morphism that is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and induces a finite extension $k(C)\subseteq k(E)$ of function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Then $p$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] at every point of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0AB6 (lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1), condition (1) and proof: a locally finite-type morphism over a one-dimensional Noetherian target with finite generic residue-field extensions is quasi-finite over every target point.
